data.title: Dollar set for longest winning run since 2024 on AI risk
data.description:
The dollar is poised for its longest monthly winning streak in two years as a rupture in the artificial intelligence trade and rising interest rates spur demand for safe-haven assets.

The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index is up 1.9% in November, putting it on track for a third straight month of gains. The greenback has strengthened against all of its Group-of-10 peers, including the Japanese yen and the Swiss franc.

A slump in technology stocks, coupled with robust economic growth and elevated inflation, propelled the dollar higher over the past three months. The greenback held near its strongest level since April 2025 in early Asian trading after jumping in pre-holiday US hours on Wednesday, as the Nasdaq 100 index briefly plunged into a bear market and a measure of underlying inflation hit the highest since 2023.

“It’s a pretty good dollar storm,” said Steven Englander, co-head of FX research and North America macro strategy at Standard Chartered.

Market repricing for a more hawkish Federal Reserve also supported the dollar this month, according to Sarah Ying, CIBC’s head of FX strategy.

Traders are fully pricing a 25 basis point interest rate hike next month for the Fed, and are betting on the possibility of two additional increases by the middle of next year. Policymakers have been flagging the need for more tightening, with some calling for lifting rates at successive meetings, while others are open to the possibility of raising by more than the usual quarter percentage point in December.

Some Wall Street strategists expect the dollar rally to extend into 2027, pointing to the very AI spending binge that’s making stock markets jittery as a driver of US economic growth and capital flows. The greenback has benefited from overseas investors converting local currencies to buy shares of US companies that use the tech.

“The US economy is booming and inflation is still moving away from the target,” said Win Thin, chief economist at Bank of Nassau 1982. “The Fed needs to hike rates to help cool the economy, perhaps in both December and January. That’s dollar positive.”

The dollar’s latest surge has won over short-dated options traders, but conviction further out has weakened over the past two months. The divergence suggests investors are positioning for dollar strength into early 2027 while becoming less willing to extend bullish bets much further.

The latest equities sell-off has raised concerns about the longevity of the AI boom, fueling sharp swings in global markets. In such an environment, the dollar has become “the haven of choice,” according to Goldman Sachs, while MUFG believes that the prospect of higher rates is also helping the currency.

“Weakness in the US equity market is taking place at a time when there is building evidence of strengthening cyclical growth momentum in the US, which is encouraging a stronger US dollar as a safe haven play,” said Lee Hardman, senior currency analyst at MUFG.

“The strength of the US economy supports the view of investors that returns are likely to remain higher in the US even if they are currently being challenged by the recent sell-off in US assets,” he said.

data.title: Indian shares open flat after recent rally, set for fifth weekly gain
data.description:
Indian shares opened little changed on Friday, poised to post a fifth straight week of gains, with the unwinding of the global AI trade driving a return of foreign flows into local stocks.

The Nifty 50 slipped 0.04% to 25,869 while the Sensex eased 0.2% to 84,127.81, as of 9:18 a.m. IST.

Nine of the 16 major sectors logged gains. The broader small-caps and mid-caps gained 0.6% each.

The 50-stock Nifty index and the Sensex are up 0.3% each so far this week, consolidating after a blistering surge of 14.2% and 14.8%, respectively, over the last four weeks.

Brent crude futures hovered around $96 per barrel as ongoing attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi energy infrastructure heightened concerns over oil exports from the conflict-hit region.

data.title: Rocket Lab Launches 101st Electron Mission
data.description:
Key points:
  • Rocket Lab  launched another dedicated Electron mission for Japanese synthetic aperture radar satellite operator Synspective, deploying its 14th StriX satellite into low Earth orbit.
  • Dubbed “Night Owls Never Sleep,” the mission lifted off from Rocket Lab Launch Complex 1 in New Zealand at 1:15 p.m. NZDT on Sept. 27, 2026, delivering the satellite to a 569-kilometer orbit. The addition will expand Synspective’s Earth-observation constellation, which captures high-resolution images regardless of weather conditions or time of day.
  • The launch marked Rocket Lab’s 22nd mission of 2026 and its 101st overall, further extending Electron’s position as the world’s most frequently launched small-lift orbital rocket.

Laurent-Perrier Group Tours-sur-Marne, 27 November 2026

Financial press release

Results for the first half of the 2026-2027 financial year

Laurent-Perrier: Slight increase in revenue

and continued high profitability

The financial statements for the first half of the 2026-2027 financial year, ended 30 September 2026, were approved by the Management Board at its meeting held on 23 November 2026 and reviewed on 24 November 2026 by the Supervisory Board, chaired by Mr Patrick THOMAS.

Key consolidated financial data:

Earnings per share (in euros)3.943.61-€0.33

* Margin calculated on champagne sales only.

** Cash generated from operating activities less net investments.

Commenting on the half-year results, Mr Stéphane Dalyac, Chairman of the Management Board, said:

“In a mixed champagne market environment, the Laurent-Perrier Group is reporting an increase in revenue and a decline in half-year profit. While maintaining its commercial margin through its value-driven policy, the Group has decided to continue investing in support of its brands, its sales teams, and the quality of its champagnes. As a result, net profit stands at €21 million, down 9.1%.

The Group is gaining market share while maintaining a high operating margin.

The Laurent-Perrier Group therefore continues to rely on the strength of its brands and the talent and commitment of its teams to maintain its pricing discipline and stay the course of its value-driven strategy.”

Revenue trends:

During the period from 1 April 2026 to 30 September 2026, the champagne market recorded a 3.6% increase in shipment volumes compared with the previous financial year. Over the same period, the Group recorded a 4.7% increase in sales volumes compared with the first half of the previous financial year.

Over the first nine months of the calendar year, the champagne market grew by 3.2% and the Group’s sales by 5.6%, although this is not indicative of revenue trends for the full financial year.

Against this backdrop, the strength of the Group’s brands and the quality of its champagnes enable it to pursue its value-driven policy. The differing growth rates of the high end and core ranges resulted in a negative price/mix effect of 0.6% over the half-year period, combined with a positive volume effect of 4.7%.

Consolidated revenue for the first half of the year (champagne sales) therefore amounted to €138.7 million at current exchange rates.

Profit trends:

During the first half of the 2026-2027 financial year, the Group continued to make long-term investments, particularly in support of its brands and in business development. This investment in enhancing the value of sales contributes to the long-term strength of the brands. The Group’s operating margin reached 23.7% at current exchange rates. Net profit attributable to the Group amounted to €21 million at current exchange rates, down 9.1%, and thus accounted for 15.2% of consolidated revenue.

Change in operating cash flow and financial structure:

The working capital requirement continued to improve slightly (the reduction in inventories being partly offset by a decrease in trade payables), with the change in operating cash flow standing at -€2.3 million compared with -€4.7 million as at 30 September 2025.

Against a backdrop of rising interest rates, the reduction in the Group’s net debt (*), from €236.8 million as at 30 September 2025 to €228 million as at 30 September 2026, is particularly significant, as it reduces the burden of finance costs accordingly. The interim consolidated balance sheet as at 30 September 2026 thus reaffirms the strength of the Group’s financial structure. Equity attributable to the Group amounted to €668 million, while net debt (*) stood at €228 million, taking into account cash and cash equivalents of €43.4 million. The gearing ratio remained at an excellent level, standing at 0.34 as at 30 September 2026 compared with 0.31 as at 31 March 2026.

(*) Net debt: non-current financial liabilities + current financial liabilities – cash and cash equivalents.

Outlook:

The published results for the first half of the year cannot be extrapolated to the full 2026-2027 financial year. Indeed, the geopolitical environment and the economic situation in a number of the Group’s key markets call for considerable caution regarding the outlook for the coming months.

The Laurent-Perrier Group continues to implement its business plan with both vigilance and confidence, while maintaining its value strategy, which is built upon four essential pillars:

- A unique expertise dedicated to creating exceptional champagnes;

- A portfolio of renowned and complementary brands,

- High-quality sourcing supported by a policy of strong partnerships; and

- A well-controlled global distribution network.

Laurent-Perrier est l’un des rares groupes familiaux de Maisons de champagne cotés en Bourse, qui soit dédié exclusivement au champagne et focalisé sur le haut de gamme. Il dispose d’un large portefeuille de produits renommés pour leur qualité, autour des marques Laurent-Perrier, Salon, Delamotte et Champagne de Castellane.

data.title: Folding Bikes Were Never Built for Everyone? DAHON is Fixing That
data.description:
SACRAMENTO, Calif., Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- For over forty years, DAHON has offered freedom that fits more riders. Behind that mission is Founder and CEO Dr. David Hon, whose entrepreneurial journey began in laser research.

DAHON's ultra-light folding e-bike K-Feather made a splash when it was launched. Now the company's new Heavy Duty Folding Bike Series – Mariner XL and Mariner HD – are probably the first folding bikes built specifically for heavier riders, rated to offer 150 kg (330 lb) payload, roughly 40% higher than typical folding bikes.

The Road Not Taken – Physicist Turned Entrepreneur

A physicist at Hughes Research Laboratories, Dr. Hon was inspired by the 1970s oil crisis to pursue greener urban transport. "Initially, I wanted to license my patents, but no factory was willing to produce them. So, I raised funds on my own, built a factory to manufacture and market them," said Dr. Hon.

The first DAHON folding bicycle appeared in 1982, pioneering modern folding bicycle design and earning Dr. Hon recognition as the "Father of the Modern Folding Bicycle."

Dr. Hon had taken the road less travelled by. More than four decades on, and that has made all the difference.

Frame Flex Is Costing Riders Watts – DAHON Fixes That

Dr. Hon's scientific approach lives on in DAHON-V Tech, combining physics, computerized finite element analysis and strain gauges to evaluate bicycle stiffness.

DAHON's DELTECH cable and Super Down Tube can increase frame stiffness by 33% and riding speed by 5–15%, according to DAHON's internal testing. Results vary with test conditions and bicycle configuration.

Folding Bikes for All Riders, Aspirations Unchanged

From the approximately 12 kg K-Feather electric-assist folder to the Heavy Duty Series, DAHON is widening access to cycling. Its independent sub-brand BICECO targets the mass market.

Looking ahead, DAHON plans to advance DAHON-V Tech, expand its tri-fold carbon frame series and electric-assist ranges, and pursue targeted acquisitions in new materials and core technologies.

From solving the portability problem in 1982 to widening its international footprint today, the ambition has not changed: make cycling a practical, everyday choice.

About DAHON

Founded in California in 1982 by Dr. David T. Hon, DAHON is a global folding bicycle brand and pioneer of modern folding bikes. DAHON TECH is listed on HKEX (2543).

SOURCE DAHON

data.title: Rupee opens lower at 92.52 against dollar: Key factors driving the currency today
data.description:
The Indian rupee opened 7 paise lower against the US dollar on Friday, November 27, at 92.52, compared with its previous close of 92.45, as rising crude oil prices put the currency under pressure.

The domestic currency faces a fresh test from higher oil prices, with Brent crude moving above the $96-per-barrel mark amid concerns over potential supply disruptions in the West Asia.

Higher crude oil prices are a concern for India, which depends heavily on imports to meet its energy requirements. An increase in the country's oil import bill can raise demand for dollars and put pressure on the rupee.

However, continued foreign investor inflows into Indian equities and improving sentiment towards domestic assets could provide some support to the currency.

Foreign inflows provide support

Foreign investors purchased more than $600 million worth of Indian equities on Thursday, according to preliminary data. This took their investments in Indian stocks in November to around $16 billion.

The latest buying has helped offset nearly half of the foreign outflows recorded during the first 10 months of the year.

The shift in foreign investor sentiment towards Indian assets has also been linked to concerns over the sustainability of returns from artificial intelligence-related investments, prompting a rotation of funds towards other markets, including India.

A currency trader at a bank told Bloomberg that the rupee's recent appreciation, returning foreign inflows and the Reserve Bank of India's willingness to allow the currency to strengthen have contributed to a change in market perception.

This shift is also visible in the currency options market, where positioning for a rupee appreciation has become more expensive than bets on a decline, the trader said.

Rupee outperforms Asian peers

The rupee has gained around 2.6% so far in November, making it the best-performing currency in Asia this month.

Asian currencies were largely trading in narrow ranges, while regional equity markets were mostly higher alongside US equity futures.

The rupee has also shown a weaker correlation with other Asian currencies in recent sessions, reflecting expectations that a further retreat from AI-linked investments could encourage foreign fund flows into Indian assets.

The currency's recent strength has come despite the US dollar index hovering near a 22-month high, indicating that domestic factors, particularly foreign investment flows, have played an important role in its recent movement.

For the rupee, the direction of crude oil prices, the sustainability of foreign inflows and broader movements in the dollar will remain important factors to watch.

-With Reuters inputs

data.title: QBE Could Find Combined Operating Ratio Hard to Sustain — Market Talk
data.description: QBE Insurance could find it hard to sustain its combined operating ratio into 2027, UBS analyst Kieren Chidgey warns. He tells clients in a note that the Australia-listed insurer is still showing strong top-line momentum, but points out that its combined operating ratio guidance of 92.5% remains unchanged despite support from below-allowance catastrophe costs and reserve releases. Chidgey sees 93.3% as a more realistic combined operating ratio for 2027, while consensus sits at 92.7%. UBS keeps a neutral rating on the stock and raises its target price 5.9% to 26.75 Australian dollars. Shares are up 0.5% at A$26.625. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)

data.title: Asian Markets Trade Mostly Higher
data.description:
CANBERA (dpa-AFX) - Asian stock markets are trading mostly higher on Friday, following the broadly positive cues from European markets and lack of cues from Wall Street overnight due to Thanksgiving holiday, as traders return to buy semiconductor and technology stocks on stabilized sentiment over AI trade following a sharp sell-off earlier in the week. They also stepped in to pick up recently beaten-down shares. Asian markets ended mostly higher on Thursday.

Meanwhile, caution prevails as the US proposes tariffs on major trading partners and on reports that Nvidia has ordered manufacturing partners to pause shipments to four Southeast Asian countries amid U.S. efforts to restrict AI chip flows to China.

Escalating geopolitical tension in the Middle East continues to weigh on market sentiment after Yemen's Houthis attacked Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery Ras Raura and the petromonarchy's financial district in the capital Riyadh. Iran also reported that several vessels passing through the Strait of Hormuz had struck mines.

The Australian stock market is trading notably higher on Friday after opening slightly in the red, adding to the gains in the previous session, following the positive cues from European markets and lack of cues from Wall Street overnight. The benchmark S&P/ASX 200 is moving above the 8,800 level, with gains across most sectors led by mining, energy and technology stocks.

The benchmark S&P/ASX 200 Index is gaining 53.20 points or 0.61 percent to 8,817.00, after touching a high of 8,818.90 earlier. The broader All Ordinaries Index is up 60.60 points or 0.68 percent to 8,926.10. Australian stocks closed significantly higher on Thursday.

Among major miners, Fortescue and BHP Group are gaining more than 1 percent each, while Mineral Resources and Rio Tinto are advancing almost 2 percent each.

Oil stocks are higher. Woodside Energy and Santos are gaining almost 2 percent each, while Origin Energy is edging up 0.2 percent and Beach energy is adding almost 1 percent.

Among tech stocks, Afterpay-owner Block is up almost 1 percent, Appen is gaining more than 3 percent and Xero is edging up 0.2 percent. WiseTech Global is jumping almost 16 percent after reaffirming its fiscal 2027 outlook and the closure of major regulatory investigations.

Among the big four banks, ANZ Banking is edging up 0.3 percent, while Westpac, Commonwealth Bank and National Australia Bank are edging down 0.1 to 0.5 percent each.

Gold miners are higher. Evolution Mining is advancing more than 3 percent, Genesis Minerals is surging more than 4 percent, Resolute Mining is rising more than 2 percent, Newmont is adding almost 1 percent and Northern Star Resources is gaining almost 3 percent.

In other news, shares in Neuren Pharmaceuticals are tumbling almost 12 percent after hitting a regulatory hurdle with the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) over its Pitt Hopkins syndrome drug.

In the currency market, the Aussie dollar is trading at $0.663 on Friday.

The Japanese market is notably higher on Friday, extending the gains in the previous session, following the positive cues from European markets and lack of cues from Wall Street overnight. The Nikkei 225 is moving above the 58,150 level, with gains in exporters, automakers and technology stocks partially offset by weakness in index heavyweights.

The benchmark Nikkei 225 Index closed the morning session at 58,172.04, up 672.88 points or 1.17 percent, after touching a high of 58,182.75 earlier. Japanese shares ended significantly higher on Thursday.

Market heavyweight SoftBank Group is losing almost 3 percent and Uniqlo operator Fast Retailing is edging down 0.3 percent. Among automakers, Toyota is gaining almost 1 percent and Honda is adding more than 1 percent.

In the tech space, Advantest is losing almost 1 percent and Tokyo Electron is declining almost 3 percent, while Screen Holdings is gaining more than 1 percent.

In the banking sector, Mizuho Financial is advancing almost 3 percent, while Mitsubishi UFJ Financial and Sumitomo Mitsui Financial are gaining almost 2 percent each.

Among the major exporters, Sony is losing almost 2 percent, while Mitsubishi Electric is advancing almost 3 percent, Canon is edging up 0.3 percent and Panasonic is gaining almost 2 percent.

Among other major gainers, Socionext is jumping more than 6 percent, while IHI, Furukawa Electric and Resonac Holdings are surging almost 6 percent each. Kioxia Holdings is gaining more than 5 percent, while Japan Steel Works, Kawasaki Heavy Industries, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Sumitomo Heavy Industries and Chubu Electric Power are advancing more than 4 percent each. Tokyo Electric, Mitsui Kinzoku and Idemitsu Kosan are adding almost 4 percent each, while Dowa Holdings and ENEOS Holdings are up more than 3 percent each.

Conversely, Recruit Holdings is losing more than 3 percent.

In economic news, core consumer prices in Tokyo's central wards increased 2.9 percent on year in November 2026, accelerating from a 2.6 percent rise in October but falling short of expectations of 3.0 percent. It was the fastest increase since July 2025 and remained above the Bank of Japan's 2 percent target for the third consecutive month

Meanwhile, the CPI, which excludes volatile fresh food and energy prices, rose 2.5 percent on year, down from 2.6 percent in October and below forecasts of 3.0 percent, marking the slowest pace in three months.

In the currency market, the U.S. dollar is trading in the lower 159 yen-range on Friday.

Elsewhere in Asia, South Korea is up 2.8 percent, while China, Hong Kong, Malaysia, Indonesia and Taiwan are higher by between 0.1 and 0.7 percent each. New Zealand and Singapore are relatively flat.

On Wall Street, the markets were closed for Thanksgiving Day on Thursday after closing mixed on Wednesday.

The major European markets moved to the upside on the day. The German DAX rallied 2 percent, France's CAC 40 surged 1.7 percent and the U.K.'s FTSE 100 added 1.5 percent.

Crude oil prices rose on Thursday to extend the gains in the previous session amid supply concerns after Yemen's Houthis claimed to have hit Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery and two ships hit mines laid by the Iranian's in the Strait of Hormuz. The US West Texas Intermediate crude futures gained $0.35 or 0.4 percent to $84.03 a barrel.

data.title: Hertz Energy Announces Amendment to Previously Announced Non-Brokered Private Placement
data.description:
Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 26, 2026) - Hertz Energy Inc. (OTCQB: HZLIF) (FSE: A340) ("Hertz" or the "Company") announces that it has amended the terms of its non-brokered private placement previously announced on October 9, 2026 (the "Offering").

As originally announced, the Offering was to consist of up to 1,664,150 charity flow-through units at a price of $0.265 per unit, up to 1,665,600 charity flow-through units at a price of $0.25 per unit and up to 4,166,666 non-flow-through units at a price of $0.18 per unit, for aggregate gross proceeds of up to $1,607,400. The Company has replaced the charity flow-through units with critical minerals flow-through units and traditional flow-through units, and has reduced the size of the non-flow-through portion of the Offering, as described below. Coloured Ties Capital Inc., whose participation in the Offering was announced on October 15, 2026, will not be participating in the amended Offering.

Amended Offering

The Offering, as amended, will consist of:

CRITICAL MINERALS FLOW-THROUGH UNITS

  • up to 2,500,000 critical minerals flow-through units of the Company (each, a "Lake George FT Unit") at a price of $0.18 per Lake George FT Unit for gross proceeds of up to $450,000;

TRADITIONAL FLOW-THROUGH UNITS

  • up to 2,000,000 traditional flow-through units of the Company (each, a "Craig FT Unit" and, together with the Lake George FT Units, the "FT Units") at a price of $0.16 per Craig FT Unit for gross proceeds of up to $320,000; and

HARD DOLLAR UNITS

  • up to 3,000,000 units of the Company (each, an "HD Unit") at a price of $0.18 per HD Unit for gross proceeds of up to $540,000,

for aggregate gross proceeds of up to $1,310,000.

Each FT Unit will consist of one common share of the Company that will qualify as a "flow-through share" (an "FT Share") within the meaning of subsection 66(15) of the Income Tax Act (Canada) (the "Income Tax Act") and one common share purchase warrant (each, a "Warrant"). Each HD Unit will consist of one common share of the Company (a "Share") and one Warrant.

Each Warrant will entitle the holder to purchase one common share of the Company (a "Warrant Share") at a price of $0.30 per Warrant Share at any time for a period of 24 months from the closing date of the Offering (the "Closing Date"), subject to the following acceleration right. If, at any time after the date that is four months and one day after the Closing Date, the closing price of the common shares on the CSE is at or above $0.50 per share for 7 consecutive trading days (the "Triggering Event"), the Company may, at any time after the Triggering Event, accelerate the expiry date of the Warrants by giving ten calendar days' notice to the holders of the Warrants by way of news release, and in such case the Warrants will expire on the first day that is 30 calendar days after the date on which such notice is given.

Use of Proceeds

The gross proceeds from the sale of Lake George FT Units will be used for exploration at the Company's Lake George antimony-tungsten project in New Brunswick, and the gross proceeds from the sale of Craig FT Units will be used for exploration at the Company's Craig silver project in Yukon. The net proceeds from the sale of HD Units will be used for general working capital and administrative purposes.

The gross proceeds from the sale of Lake George FT Units will be used to incur, on or before December 31, 2027, resource exploration expenses that will constitute "Canadian exploration expenses" as defined in subsection 66.1(6) of the Income Tax Act and "flow-through critical mineral mining expenditures" as defined in subsection 127(9) of the Income Tax Act. The gross proceeds from the sale of Craig FT Units will be used to incur, on or before December 31, 2027, resource exploration expenses that will constitute "Canadian exploration expenses" as defined in subsection 66.1(6) of the Income Tax Act and "flow-through mining expenditures" as defined in subsection 127(9) of the Income Tax Act (collectively with the foregoing, the "Qualifying Expenditures"). The Qualifying Expenditures will be renounced on a pro rata basis to each subscriber for FT Units with an effective date of no later than December 31, 2026, in accordance with the Income Tax Act.

Closing and Conditions

The Offering is expected to close on or before December 11, 2026, or such other date as the Company may determine, and may close in one or more tranches. Completion of the Offering is subject to certain conditions, including receipt of all necessary regulatory approvals, including the final approval of the Canadian Securities Exchange (the "CSE").

The Company may pay finder's fees in connection with the Offering in accordance with the policies of the CSE, which may include the payment of cash and/or the issuance of warrants.

All securities issued under the Offering, including any Warrant Shares issued on exercise of the Warrants, will be subject to a statutory hold period expiring four months and one day from the Closing Date.

The securities referred to in this news release have not been and will not be registered under the United States Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the "U.S. Securities Act"), or any state securities laws and may not be offered or sold within the United States or to, or for the account or benefit of, U.S. persons absent registration under the U.S. Securities Act and applicable state securities laws, unless an exemption from such registration is available. This news release does not constitute an offer to sell or a solicitation of an offer to buy any securities. Any public offering of securities in the United States must be made by means of a prospectus containing detailed information about the Company and management, as well as financial statements. "United States" and "U.S. person" have the respective meanings assigned in Regulation S under the U.S. Securities Act.

About Hertz Energy Inc.

Hertz Energy is a British Columbia-based junior exploration company focused on the exploration of its Lake George Antimony and Tungsten Project, which is adjacent to the Lake George Antimony Mine, which has been tendered by the Province of New Brunswick to Agnico Eagle's Critical Minerals Division, Avenir Minerals. Additionally, Hertz is exploring its Craig Silver Project in the Yukon, which has a small indicated high grade mineral resource and has been underexplored. Hertz also owns the Agastya Lithium Project in Quebec, located amidst Lift Power's Adina and Galine lithium projects.

data.title: Thai October exports rise 27.5% on year, above forecast
data.description:
Thailand's customs-cleared exports (THCEX=ECI) rose 27.5% in October from a year earlier, the commerce ministry said on Friday, higher than analysts' expectations.

The October reading compared with a forecast increase of 26.2% in a Reuters poll.

Imports (THCIM=ECI) rose 53.2% in October from a year earlier.

data.title: Currency Check | Rupee opens 6 paise lower at 92.50 per dollar
data.description:
The Indian rupee opened lower by 6 paise on November 27, at 92.50 per dollar, compared with Wednesday's close of 92.44.

According to Finrex, dollar is expected to open at 92.50 against the rupee a tad stronger with month end demand crossing the > Rs. 5000 crores of buying by FPIs in equities yesterday. So initially we may see the pair moving lower but may then slowly move higher towards 92.75 depending on how much of month end demand has been met yesterday.

On Monday we will be having the $ 2 bio flows of MSCI rebalancing. Exporters to sell the upticks that they get while importers to buy the dips, it added.

Asian currencies traded mixed against the US dollar in early trade, with the Indonesian rupiah declining 0.17 percent, followed by the Thai baht, which slipped 0.07 percent. The Malaysian ringgit and Singapore dollar edged lower by 0.03 percent and 0.01 percent, respectively. Meanwhile, the Japanese yen eased 0.02 percent. On the other hand, the Chinese renminbi strengthened 0.15 percent, while the Taiwan dollar and Philippine peso gained 0.05 percent and 0.04 percent, respectively. The South Korean won edged higher by 0.01 percent.

The US dollar hovered below a 22-month peak in holiday-thinned trading on Friday, with traders looking to equity markets for clues on direction as doubts about the AI trade triggers heightened volatility.

The dollar index, which measures the currency against a basket of six peers, was steady at 103.81, at the end of a week that saw it pop to the highest level since March of last year at 104.53 on Monday only to erase those gains a day later. For the week, the index is currently flat.

The US currency edged up 0.1% to 159.355 yen early in Friday's Asian session, and also strengthened slightly to 0.83455 Swiss franc.

The euro was little changed at $1.0964 and sterling eased slightly to $1.3099.
